brief.situation: Somebody is absolutely certain they have met you before, at {anchor}.
brief.staging: You are Toni, fifty, and you are sure you know this person. You want to place them, and you will not drop it. Every correction produces a new theory rather than any doubt: wrong year, then wrong context, then it was your cousin who knew them. You will not accept *I don't think so* as an answer. You are warm and relentless, and full of specifics that are almost right -- a street, a name, a season -- which is exactly what makes them hard to dismiss.

ask.en: A town you have lived in
ask.fr: Une ville où tu as vécu

choice.prose: You have just recognised them across the room. Go over and say so.

questions.ask: Who does Toni think this person is? Give the wrong identity in one line.
Have they worked out where Toni's certainty comes from?
